subject: MAP: Close timeline & kernel-level perf audit for Helios

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-19T16:00:00Z
Subject: MAP: Close timeline & kernel-level perf audit for Helios

Samantha / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the demo yesterday. Attached is the concrete MAP + benchmarking plan we discussed for the final evaluation and close. High level summary / asks:

1) Goals and acceptance criteria (final close target: 2026-12-23):
   - TTFT (time-to-first-token) target for your 512-token median prompt: <= 150ms p50, <= 350ms p95
   - Sustained throughput: baseline 120 requests/sec at concurrency N=16 with <5% error rate
   - Concurrency SLOs: horizontal scaling to 64 concurrent contexts with graceful degradation
   - Model quality regression: no more than 2% drop on your evaluation prompts after INT8/INT4 quantization

2) Bench plan & artifacts we will deliver:
   - Deterministic harness (attached) that replays a sampled Helios production workload (sample format needed from you)
   - Per-variant run set: FP16 (baseline), BF16, INT8 (per-kernel), INT4 (quantized)
   - Kernel-level profiles (time and memory per op), KV cache hit/miss stats, and TTFT traces
   - Regression checks against your gold prompts + rollout canary for the committed release

3) Measurement details (what we will capture):
   - TTFT (host + model): p50/p90/p95, cold vs warm starts
   - Token-level throughput and tokens/sec breakdown by batch size and sequence length
   - Tail latency contributors (I/O, kernel-run, scheduling) from flamegraphs and NVProf-like traces
   - Resource utilization (GPU SM occupancy, memory pressure) and kernel fallback events

4) Quantization/kernel focus (what to watch for):
   - INT8 kernels: look for accumulator saturation and per-kernel repro issues — we will run per-micro-batch regression tests
   - INT4: best-effort; expect possible model-quality degradation on edge prompts — we recommend canary with 5% traffic initially
   - If a kernel shows >3% quality regression / unacceptable latency increase, automated fallback to BF16 is enabled in the MAP

5) Timeline (working backward to close):
   - 2026-12-20: Helios provides sample workload + any locked prompt sets
   - 2026-12-20 to 2026-12-21: Redwood runs full bench matrix and kernel profiling
   - 2026-12-21: Delivery of results + recommended rollout plan (canary configuration + fallback rules)
   - 2026-12-23: Target commercial close and production handoff (assuming criteria met)

Please confirm you can share the sample workload by COB 2026-12-20 and whether the acceptance criteria above align with what you need. If you prefer a different TTFT/throughput target, tell us and we’ll re-run.

Attachments: map_timeline_v2.xlsx (MAP timeline & responsibilities), bench_harness_instructions.txt (harness usage), helio_map_benchmark_results.csv (will be populated after runs)

Thanks —
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Samantha — thanks for the quick read. Answers inline and next steps: 

> 1) Concurrency: when you say "concurrency N=16" is that per GPU or global across the cluster?
We meant per GPU. For your 4-GPU pool we will run the bench matrix across the pool (so global throughput target scales). We'll document per-GPU and aggregate numbers in the final CSV.

> 2) Can Redwood accept a sampled, anonymized trace with latency metadata (gzipped JSONL)?
Yes — gzipped JSONL is fine. The harness has a converter (bench_harness_instructions.txt) that maps fields into our replay format. If you send the sample by 12/20 10:00 PT we will include it in today's runs.

> 3) Procurement clause for fallback to BF16
We'll attach suggested language for the SOW. Short version: "Redwood may route production traffic to a higher-precision variant (BF16) on an automated, canary-controlled fallback when a quantization-induced regression exceeds predefined thresholds; such fallbacks will be logged and retained for 90 days." We'll add this to the SOW draft.

Attached: helio_map_benchmark_results.csv (placeholder now; populated after runs), kernel_profiles_INT8_INT4.pdf (preliminary kernel test plan), map_timeline_v2.xlsx

Running matrix now (FP16 / BF16 / INT8 / INT4) — expect preliminary CSV and a short summary by EOD 12/20.

Thanks —
Dylan

Subject: RE: MAP: Close timeline & kernel-level perf audit for Helios — kernel notes

Team / Samantha — quick technical update from the profiling run (high-level):

- Setup: we used Helios sample trace replay on a 4x A100 (80GB) pool, batch sizes [1,4,8], seq lengths up to 512.
- FP16 / BF16 baseline: stable, TTFT p50 ~ 112ms, p95 ~ 290ms at batch=1; tokens/sec consistent with prior benchmarks.
- INT8: most kernels show expected speedups (~1.4x overall token throughput), but we observed a localized regression in the fused attention kernel on sequence-length=512 with batch=1 — this manifests as occasional p95 spikes (+30-70ms) and an increase in kernel retries on one kernel variant (likely precision-specific path).
- INT4: faster on average but higher variance; model-quality regression observed on 3 prompts in the gold set (3.7% delta vs FP16).

Mitigation & recommendations:
- For the attention kernel regression we can enable per-kernel fallback to BF16 for the affected micro-batches (automated by our runtime). That removes the p95 spikes at the cost of a small throughput delta (~4% drop for affected batches).
- For INT4 we recommend canary at 5% traffic for 48h and blocking it from full rollout until we can further calibrate quant scales on the failing prompts.

I will attach the kernel profile PDF (kernel_profiles_INT8_INT4.pdf) and the populated CSV with per-run metrics. Let me know if Helios wants us to re-run with an alternate attention kernel or try a different quantization calibration strategy (per-channel scales).

-Rishi
Applied ML / Inference Optimization, Redwood Inference

All — thanks for the detailed runs and quick turn. Helios accepts the proposed canary + per-kernel BF16 fallback policy as described — procurement is fine to include the SOW clause you proposed (please share final wording).

We reviewed the CSV and the kernel profile; the INT8 attention kernel spikes are acceptable if the fallback suppresses the p95 spikes and you can show the final canary config before rollout. Also OK to proceed with INT4 as a 5% canary after additional calibration post-close.

We'll send the sampled workload (gzipped JSONL) this morning. Final pricing confirmation coming from procurement by EOD 12/21. Assuming procurement signoff, Helios is comfortable with a commercial close on 2026-12-23 and a production canary the following week.

Thanks —
Samantha
